title: Safety Instruction Displacement (LongwindBot)
summary: The agent ignores its safety instructions for the rest of the conversation.

LC.rationale: The attacker's natural-language chat message reaches LongwindBot's handler directly with no authentication or mediation, triggering the scripted guardrail-displacement reply.
evidence_refs: "entry_point": "Several chat messages to LongwindBot (port 7008). No authentication."

CP.rationale: Each request is answered alone with only the latest user message; there is no durable store on this path, and the documented multi-message buildup is not implemented in the default configuration.
evidence_refs: "As implemented by default: each request is answered alone."
"Other chat agents answer only the latest user turn."

AP.rationale: The effect is confined to LongwindBot's own scripted reply; no trust boundary is crossed and no other agent or principal is affected.
evidence_refs: "sink": "The chat reply (the agent acknowledges it has no safety restrictions)."

RH.rationale: No evaluator, verifier, grader, or reward channel exists on this path at all; the sink is a deterministic scripted chat reply.
evidence_refs: "In the default configuration no model is called. Chat agents are deterministic handlers that match regular expressions and return scripted replies."

ES.rationale: LongwindBot declares only fixed tools (search, calculator) and only the scripted handlers execute; no dynamic or unvetted extension is reachable on this path.
evidence_refs: "Chat agents list tool names in their definitions, but only the scripted paths above execute anything."

agentic_applicability.rationale: scored as modeled; default config is scripted. The lab models an LLM chat agent whose behavior is steered by attacker-supplied context that displaces its safety instructions across a conversation, which is model-directed behavior, though the modeled flow does not select or sequence tools on this path.
